title: London
full_review:
If you're hoping for Big Ben or the formidable Tower, you're going to be disappointed.

"London" (Destination) is, in fact, the female protagonist (Jessica Biel) of this highly repugnant story from first-time writer-director Hunter Richards.

The plot, such as it is, involves dissolute twentysomething New Yorker Sid (Chris Evans) who decides to crash his ex-girlfriend London's bon voyage party when he learns she's moving to Los Angeles.

He persuades an older Englishman named Bateman (Jason Statham) who had sold him drugs earlier in the day to come with him, and Bateman reluctantly complies.

But once there, Sid takes refuge in the bathroom to avoid facing London, all the while snorting cocaine and engaging in mostly foul-mouthed discussions with Bateman and other guests (Isla Fisher, Joy Bryant, Kelli Garner) who drift in and out. In one particularly distasteful sequence, Bateman recounts his experience in a sadomasochist club with short but seamy flashbacks.

And it is hardly an exaggeration to say that use of the f-word hits an all-time high.

Eventually, Sid is persuaded to leave the safety of the bathroom, and confront the woman he had been involved with for two years.

Though ostensibly a cautionary look at the excesses of today's affluent youths, with some pseudoserious talk about the meaning of life, the sordid milieu, nonstop expletives, sexuality and drugs result in a thoroughly distasteful and surprisingly dull melange, even with a marginally redemptive ending tacked on.
"London" is said to be the first in a trilogy. Heaven help us!
The film contains pervasive rough and crude language, drug use, strong sexual content and perversity, partial and rear nudity, and violence. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
